correctness.rationale: In a period of distinct letter runs every nonunary factor has a unique cyclic phase; only the terminal marker creates mixed right branches. Classifying short unary branches and the two repeated-suffix extensions gives exactly \(2q+1\) distinct supermaximal extensions. Their ending sets are pairwise disjoint, the 2q-1 short sets have k positions apiece, and the two long sets are singletons. Suffix coverage and a pigeonhole lower bound give the complete minimum-set bijection and count \(k^{2q-1}\). Choosing the terminal and q first-period run boundaries gives the sharp string-attractor size q+1. The standalone literal right-extension enumeration reproduces all predictions for 246 parameter tuples and directly enumerates four minimum-set families; finite tests are supporting checks, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The measure counts positions needed for compressed pattern indexing. For a family with arbitrary alphabet size and independent run lengths, the theorem supplies the complete set of optimal suffixient position choices and exact product count, not only an optimum bound. The stable count despite arbitrary large runs quantifies redundant indexing choices, and the sharp \(q\)-position gap from string attractors shows a genuine structural difference on the same text. This is a motivated natural periodic-family classification, not a lone small parameter value.
